components.text: Whether religious persistence and content can be explained primarily as culturally copied meme complexes.
Whether beneficial religious elements can arise from patterns deeper than interpersonal cultural copying.
Explain religious persistence and beneficial religious patterns as culturally copied meme-complex effects.
Whether biological archetypes displace memes as an explanation of culturally transmitted religious material.
Whether copied cultural variants constitute a causally distinct replication process layered upon genes.
Show that biologically deep archetypes displace or invalidate a distinct cultural-copying explanation.
Whether biblical responses to suffering warrant implications of divine causation or deserved suffering.
Whether practical narrative depth can be accepted while retaining an evolutionary explanation of painful childbirth.
Establish what follows from biblical stories addressing suffering, tragedy, and malevolence.
Whether accepting biblical wisdom justifies an implication of divine causation for suffering.
Whether biblical texts can be culturally foundational even if a literal divine-causation reading is rejected.
Distinguish the usefulness of biblical narratives from any implication of divine causation or deserved suffering.
Whether abandoning inherited religious foundations predictably produces nihilism, disorder, or totalitarian substitution.
Whether cross-society and cross-state social outcomes fit the predicted relationship between religiosity and stability.
Show that removing inherited religious foundations predictably creates nihilism, disorder, or totalitarian substitutes.
Whether gratitude and value-laden conduct require a functional divine object or religious highest commitment.
Whether secular contemplative practice can independently generate grateful orientation and constructive conduct.
Show that apparently secular conduct or valuation still depends on something functioning as God.
Whether secular gratitude can genuinely lack an object occupying the functional place attributed to God.
Whether phenomenological absence of a particular recipient settles the structure of the underlying psychological hierarchy.
Establish that gratitude can arise through secular practice without being directed toward God.
Whether secular reflection and meditation can support gratitude without God.
Whether positive affect or happiness is sufficient as the ultimate orientation of human action.
Show that secular contemplative practice can support gratitude and a positive orientation without God.
Whether humans require ultimate, tragedy-sustaining meaning in order to remain motivated and live positively.
Whether evolved needs continue to generate ordinary action after ultimate cosmic meaning is rejected.
Show that action requires meaning deep enough to sustain human beings through tragedy.
Whether ordinary evolved needs leave action ultimately meaningless despite continuing to motivate local behavior.
Whether coordinating needs across time and with others generates genuinely higher-order meanings from proximal purposes.
Explain how evolved creatures can live positively and continue acting despite ultimate meaninglessness.
Whether higher meanings emerging from coordinated purposes require religious grounding rather than cultural construction.
Whether biological dispositions and memetic layers jointly explain the formation of higher-order meanings.
Show that coordinating biological needs across time and society generates nonarbitrary higher meanings.
Whether prosocial atheist conduct may be reclassified as implicitly religious under a functional definition of God.
Whether conduct should override a person's explicit self-description when attributing religious belief.
Whether the functional account explains why a professed atheist behaves morally rather than merely renaming that behavior.
Establish that prosocial conduct reveals an implicitly religious highest commitment despite an atheist's stated profession.
